records.name: Hodosan Shrine
records.description: An ancient Shinto shrine founded around 110 AD at the foot of Mount Hodo, dedicated to safeguarding against natural disasters. The shrine features Gongen-zukuri architectural style with vibrantly colored carvings and is believed to bring luck with money and matchmaking. It is one of Chichibu's three primary shrines and was recognized with a Michelin Green Guide Japan star.
records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (10-15 minute walk)

records.name: Hodosan Ropeway
records.description: A scenic gondola line that carries visitors up Mount Hodo (497 meters) to the summit in approximately 5 minutes, covering a distance of 832 meters. The ropeway offers panoramic views of Chichibu and operates with two historic cabins nicknamed 'Bambi' and 'Monkey' after local wildlife. It provides access to gardens, shrines, hiking trails, and a small animal park at the summit.

tips.text: Tickets are cash-only (no card payment) and must be purchased at the gate. Round-trip adult tickets cost 1,200 yen; children under 12 are 600 yen; infants under 3 ride free.
The ropeway operates on different schedules for weekdays (once every 30 minutes) and weekends (once every 15 minutes). During peak seasons, the schedule extends to 5:20 PM.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (20 minute walk to base station)

records.name: Nagatoro Iwadatami Rocks
records.description: A stunning geological formation along the Arakawa River consisting of layered crystalline schist rocks spanning 80 meters wide and 500 meters long. The rocks resemble overlapping tatami mats and were created by ancient tectonic activity and river erosion. This 6-kilometer valley section is designated as a nationally recognized place of scenic beauty and natural monument.

tips.text: Wooden-boat cruises operate along the Iwadatami rocks from March to December (9:00-16:00). Courses last about 20 minutes and offer calm scenic rides or thrilling rapid sections.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (5 minute walk via Iwadatami Dori)

records.name: Saitama Museum of Natural History
records.description: A prefectural natural history museum opened in 1981 displaying fossils, rocks, minerals, plants, and animals collected in Saitama Prefecture. Notable exhibits include the skeleton of the extinct giant shark 'Megalodon' and the mysterious marine animal 'Paleoparadoxia'. The museum features geology and biology exhibitions with interactive dioramas and tactile displays suitable for all ages.

tips.text: A maple forest outside the museum features almost all species of naturally grown maple trees in Saitama, beautifully illuminated at night during autumn.

records.station: Kami-Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (5 minute walk)

records.name: Tsukinoishi Momiji Park
records.description: A celebrated autumn foliage viewing spot featuring approximately 50 Japanese maple trees (acer amoenum). Named after a stone tablet inscribed with a famous haiku by poet Kyoshi Takahama, the park is renowned for its mystical beauty and attracts over 20,000 visitors annually. It is beautifully illuminated at night during peak autumn season in mid-November.

tips.text: Best viewing time is around November when autumn leaves reach peak color. The park is illuminated in the evenings during peak foliage season.

records.station: Kami-Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (3-5 minute walk)

records.name: Nagatoro Town Museum (Arai Silkworm House)
records.description: A museum displaying silkworm culture and farming implements collected from Nagatoro Town. Adjacent to the museum is the Historic Arai Silkworm House, an approximately 250-270 year-old traditional Edo-period residence of a silk farmer designated as a National Important Cultural Property. The house features a distinctive shingle roof with layers of chestnut boards weighted by stones.
records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (10 minute walk)

records.name: Fudoji Temple
records.description: A Shingon Buddhist temple located at the foot of Mount Hodo, and one of Nagatoro's Seven Flower Temples. The temple is renowned for its spectacular cherry blossoms, featuring approximately 500 yaezakura (double cherry) trees of about 30 different varieties planted on the grounds. The 'Street Cherry Blossoms' course around the temple is illuminated at night during peak bloom.

tips.text: Peak bloom for the 'Street Cherry Blossoms' at Fudoji is mid-April to late April. The temple grounds display rare cherry tree varieties with name boards identifying each type.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway

records.name: Hozenji Temple
records.description: A historic temple in Nagatoro notable for its early cherry blossoms. The temple features the 'Yida no Sakura' (Yida Cherry), an old weeping cherry tree that blooms earlier than most trees in the area, typically in late March. It is one of the notable cherry blossom viewing spots in Nagatoro's extensive hanami (cherry blossom) season.
records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway

records.name: Kita Sakura-dori (North Cherry Blossom Street)
records.description: A 2.5-4 kilometer cherry blossom tunnel lined with approximately 400-1500 Somei Yoshino cherry trees stretching from Nagatoro Station to Takasago Bridge (near Nogami Station) along the Arakawa River. The street offers an immersive hanami experience with evening illuminations from late March to early April. Nagatoro has been designated one of Japan's Top 100 Cherry Blossom Viewing Sites.

tips.text: Best viewing time is early-mid April. Evening illuminations run from late March to early April. The street is very busy during peak season.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway
records.address: Nagatoro to Takasago Bridge, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Minami Sakura-dori (South Cherry Blossom Street)
records.description: A 1.5-3 kilometer cherry blossom tunnel lined with approximately 200-400 cherry trees on both sides, running from Kami-Nagatoro Station to Nagatoro Station. This secondary cherry blossom viewing route features Somei Yoshino and other cherry varieties and complements the larger Kita Sakura-dori avenue as part of Nagatoro's extensive spring blooms.
records.station: Kami-Nagatoro Station or Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway
records.address: Kami-Nagatoro Station to Nagatoro Station, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Mount Hodo
records.description: A 497-meter mountain dominating the Nagatoro landscape offering scenic hiking trails and panoramic views of the surrounding Chichibu region. The mountain features various seasonal displays including cherry blossoms in spring, autumn foliage, and wintersweet gardens in winter. Multiple trails provide access, with the fastest route taking 1 hour 20 minutes from base to summit.

tips.text: Well-maintained hiking trails make Mount Hodo accessible even for beginners. The Hodosan Ropeway provides an easier 5-minute ascent alternative.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (20 minute walk to base)

records.name: Hodosan Shrine Okumiya (Rear Shrine)
records.description: The inner shrine of Hodosan Shrine located at the summit of Mount Hodo (497 meters). Accessible via the Hodosan Ropeway or hiking trail, this mountain shrine offers panoramic views of the Nagatoro Valley and surrounding Chichibu mountains. The shrine and surrounding area feature seasonal flower displays and serve as a spiritual site for mountain worship in the Kanto region.
records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (reach via ropeway or hiking)
records.address: Summit of Mount Hodo, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Mt. Hodo Umehyakkaen (Plum Garden)
records.description: A plum garden at the summit of Mount Hodo featuring approximately 470 plum trees of about 170 different varieties. Planting began in 1986, showcasing rare varieties such as early-blooming red plums and the three famous 'moon-viewing' plums. The fragrant plum scent spreads across the summit from mid-February onward, providing a scenic display of pink and white blossoms.

tips.text: Peak bloom for plum blossoms is from mid-February onward. Best viewing is usually at the end of January or early February for maximum fragrance and color.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (20 minute walk + ropeway or hiking)
records.address: Summit of Mount Hodo, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Hodosan Wintersweet Garden (Robaien)
records.description: A wintersweet garden on Mount Hodo featuring approximately 800 wintersweet plants (about 3,000 blossoms) blooming from late December to late February. The garden is filled with fragrant yellow blossoms and offers panoramic views of Chichibu's cityscape and mountains including Mount Bukō and surrounding ranges. One of the finest viewing locations in the Kanto region.

tips.text: Best viewing is usually at the end of January or early February. Free shuttle bus service runs from the station on weekends and holidays during the wintersweet festival season.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (20 minute walk + ropeway or hiking)
records.address: Summit of Mount Hodo, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Hodosan Small Animal Zoo
records.description: A small zoo at the summit of Mount Hodo featuring Japanese macaques (monkeys) and deer, the animals after which the Hodosan Ropeway's gondolas are named ('Bambi' and 'Monkey'). The zoo is accessible via the ropeway or hiking trail and provides an interactive wildlife experience within the scenic mountain setting.

tips.text: The zoo is open year-round but may close during ropeway inspection periods. Call ahead to confirm operating status.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (via ropeway or hiking trail)
records.address: Summit of Mount Hodo, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Susabino Terrace
records.description: A scenic observation terrace opened in July 2025 at the summit of Mount Hodo. The terrace features sky-view benches, panoramic counter seats, open-air sofas, and photo spots with mountain monument views. Visitors can enjoy expansive views of Mount Bukō, the Chichibu mountain range, and the Nagatoro Valley, with seasonal beauty and fragrant wintersweet in winter.
records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (via ropeway + 5 minute walk)
records.address: Summit of Mount Hodo, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: California Poppy Garden (Hanabishisou-en)
records.description: A garden featuring California poppies (golden poppies) covering approximately 10,000 square meters of land behind the Nagatoro Town Museum. In early summer, typically mid-May through mid-June, the hillside blooms with vibrant orange flowers creating a stunning contrast against the deep blue sky. The garden name comes from the rhombus-like shape of the poppy flower.

tips.text: Peak bloom time is mid-May to mid-June. Best visiting hours are morning to mid-afternoon to see the flowers fully open.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (8 minute walk)

records.name: SL Paleo Express (Steam Locomotive)
records.description: A historic steam locomotive built in 1944, known as 'the closest steam locomotive to central Tokyo.' Operated by Chichibu Railway, the Paleo Express runs one round trip daily between Kumagaya and Mitsumineguchi stations (71.7 kilometers, approximately 2 hours 40 minutes). Passengers can experience the sights, sounds, and smells of vintage steam travel while passing through scenic Chichibu landscapes including Nagatoro.

tips.text: Seats are available by reservation only. Booking in advance is essential, especially for popular dates. Reservations can be made online through the Chichibu Railway SL Reservation System (Japanese only) or at stations.
In addition to the regular fare, a reserved seat ticket (1,100 yen for adults and children) is required. Operating dates may change; check the official Chichibu Railway website.

records.hours: Weekends and holidays, March 20-December 6 (with some weekday exceptions)
records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (stops 11:33-11:42 AM and 3:07-3:13 PM)
records.address: Operates on Chichibu Railway Chichibu Main Line, multiple stations including Nagatoro

records.name: Nagatoro Station
records.description: A historic wooden train station built in 1911 and designated as a significant architectural landmark. The station features nostalgic design and remains largely unchanged since its opening, preserving early 20th-century railway architecture. It serves as the main gateway to Nagatoro and offers excellent vantage points for photographing the scenic surroundings and passing trains, including the SL Paleo Express.

tips.text: The station stops the SL Paleo Express for approximately 10 minutes, providing excellent time to photograph the locomotive and surrounding cherry blossoms in spring.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway

records.name: Iwadatami-dori Shopping Street
records.description: A charming 400-meter-long traditional shopping street running from the river boat embarkation point back toward Nagatoro Station. The winding thoroughfare is filled with souvenir shops and local retail establishments selling regional specialties and crafts. It provides a cultural immersion in Nagatoro's historic tourist district.

tips.text: Local specialty items sold include soba and udon noodles, pickled mountain vegetables, walnuts, and small sun-dried vegetables.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (5 minute walk downhill)

records.name: Nagatoro Valley (Nagatoro Gorge)
records.description: A scenic 6-kilometer stretch of the Arakawa River valley designated as a nationally recognized place of scenic beauty and natural monument. The valley features dramatic rock formations, the famous Iwadatami layered rocks, and towering river cliffs. It showcases the formative beauty of nature created by tectonic changes and river erosion, offering spectacular views that change seasonally with cherry blossoms in spring and autumn foliage in fall.

tips.text: The valley offers multiple ways to experience its beauty: by boat cruise along the Arakawa River, by hiking riverside trails, or by viewing from the Kita Sakura-dori and other scenic roads.

records.station: Nagatoro Station or surrounding stations, Chichibu Railway

records.name: Hodosan Approach (Cherry Blossom-Lined Path)
records.description: An approximately 800-meter uphill road leading to the entrance of Hodosan Shrine, lined with cherry trees of 30 different varieties. During spring cherry blossom season (early to mid-April), the path creates a picturesque tunnel of blossoms. The approach features illuminations during the blooming season, creating magical nighttime views distinct from daytime scenery.

tips.text: Peak bloom is early to mid-April. Evening illuminations run from late March to early April, creating a different magical atmosphere compared to daytime viewing.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (15 minute walk)
records.address: Leading to Hodosan Shrine, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Arakawa River Boat Cruises
records.description: Traditional Japanese wooden boat cruises down the Arakawa River operating for over 100 years. Skilled boatmen using long poles navigate passengers through scenic canyons with dramatic rock formations and river rapids. The cruises operate from March to December with both calm scenic routes and thrilling rapid sections. In winter, heated kotatsu boats are available for a cozy riverside experience.

tips.text: Advance reservations are highly recommended, especially during peak seasons. Online booking can reduce wait times that may exceed 3 hours. Boats operate on schedules roughly every 5-20 minutes.
Course A and B (3 km, approximately 20 minutes) cost around 2,000 yen for adults. Courses offer different experiences: calm scenic rides or thrilling sections through white-water rapids.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (5 minute walk to Iwadatami Dori)
records.address: Iwadatami boat landing, Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Seven Flower Temples (Autumn Flower Circuit)
records.description: A network of seven temples throughout Nagatoro, each associated with one of the seven flowers of autumn: bush clover, Japanese pampas grass, kudzu, fringed pink, golden lace, thoroughwort, and Chinese bellflower. The Japanese people have appreciated these flowers since ancient times. A pilgrimage tour visiting all seven temples by hiking or bicycle rental provides cultural immersion and botanical exploration throughout the town.

tips.text: A complete tour of the Seven Flower Temples is recommended by hiking or using rental bicycles. The pilgrimage provides both spiritual and nature-viewing experiences.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway
records.address: Multiple locations throughout Nagatoro, Nagatoro-machi, Chichibu-gun, Saitama

records.name: Nagatoro Tourist Information Center
records.description: The main tourism information center for Nagatoro, offering multilingual information sheets and resources for planning visits. The center is located near Nagatoro Station and provides rental bicycles (including electric-powered models) for exploring the town's attractions. Staff can assist with itinerary planning and provide maps and guidance.

tips.text: Free English-language information sheets are available. Bicycle rentals (including electric bikes) can be arranged here, providing an efficient way to cover Nagatoro's attractions.

records.station: Nagatoro Station, Chichibu Railway (adjacent to station)
